page.layout: One printed page: one column of running text, with one marginal note in the right margin beside line 19. Page number top right. Running head top centre. Catchword "qui" bottom right.

main_text.p: cerit tandem ad ipsorum exemplar per vitam Regis jurare; quomodo solitæ sunt posterioribus seculis Romani ex adulatione quadam jurare per genium Impera-toris. Sed non facile me patior de diuinis factisque insignium pietate virorum æquius judicare quam res ipsa cogit. Video veterum plerosque ita Sanctorum famæ detulisse, ut ingenio suo nimium indulserint, dum eorum a-pertos lapsus honesto aliquo velamine excusare conantur. Errore· saltem aliquanto honestiore, quam est error eorum, qui postremo hoc seculo amant a diverso in piorum virorum lapsus curiosius inquirere, & ne desit quod calumniantur, vel recte facta pervertendo singerum vas incrustare gestiunt. Mitius aliquanto alii Josephi dictum illud inter-Opin. 2.pretantur: eum sc,quo tectius rem gereret ne fratribus alicunde forte suboleret quis esset, ni Ægyptiaci principis quam induerat personam perite sustineret, formulam hanc jurandi Aulicis regiis familiarem, illa tantum vice in compendium simulationis adhibuisse. At mihi non est volupe[?] vel hanc culpam, etsi paulo leviorem, sanctissimo viro impingere sine necessitate. Tertia est eorum sententia, qui

page.notes: Left edge of the scan is cut: the first letters of several lines are partly lost (e.g. "pertos", "rum", "iquanto"); I read them from the context and the continuing words. "fc,quo tectius" in the line "pretantur: eum" is doubtful; the printed form may be a variant of "sed quo tectius". "volupe" at the line start is clipped and may be read as "volupe" or a fuller word. The raised dot after "Errore" is a printer's mark, kept as "·". A small asterisk stands beside the last line above "qui"; it is a printer's mark and not a note. The "a-" / "pertos" and "Impera-" / "toris" breaks keep their printed hyphens.
